title: Protocol for ex vivo culture of patient-derived tumor fragments
protocol: Collect tumor tissue in ice-cold sterile tumor collection medium.
Keep the collected tumor tissue on ice during transport.
Store tumor samples for a maximum of 1 hour at 4°C in collection medium if necessary.
Prepare necessary items for tumor tissue processing.
Cut tumor tissue into smaller sections of 4-5 cm.
Place unprocessed tissue sections either on petri dishes or in tubes until processing.
Process tumor tissue into PDTFs (Pieces Dissociated Tumor Fragments) in medium.
Transfer processed PDTFs to a tube containing medium.
Store prepared PDTFs in liquid nitrogen for long-term storage.
Prepare aliquots of 5 mL tumor collection medium in a sterile 50 mL tube and store until usage at 4°C.
Collect the tumor material in the 50 mL tube and keep on ice until processing.
Transfer the tumor tissue from the 50 mL tube in a small volume of collection medium to the petri dish on ice.
Cut tumor tissue into pieces of approximately 1 mm3 using a sharp scalpel.
Keep cut tumor pieces on ice either in collection medium in the petri dish or submerged in the 50 mL tube to avoid drying out.
Process each piece of the tumor tissue until it has been cut into PDTFs (Primary Dissected Tumor Fragments) while keeping them covered with collection medium.
Remove any necrotic parts and blood coagulates from the tumor.
Assess the tumor material by a pathologist before processing.
Mix PDTFs from different regions and pieces to ensure uniform representation of the tumor lesion.
Gather 8–15 fragments in small heaps on the petri dish.
Label round bottom cryovials.
Add 1 mL of freezing medium to each vial.
Transfer 8–15 fragments to each cryovial by putting them against the wall on top.
Close all the lids and flip the tubes to immerse all fragments into the freezing medium.
Tap the tubes to ensure fragments are not sticking onto each other.
Store cryovials in a freezing container at -80°C freezer.
Maintain a consistent -1 °C/min freezing rate for the fragments.
Transfer cryovials to a liquid nitrogen tank after reaching -80°C and store until further use.
Cut collected tumor tissue into smaller sections.
Keep tumor sections in the dish or in 50 mL tube containing collection medium.
Process each section into PDTFs of 1 mm³.
Mix all processed tumor fragments to ensure uniform representation of the tumor tissue.
Thaw Matrigel for 12 hours on ice at 4°C the day before starting the ex vivo culture.
Pre-cool pipette tips at 4°C before use.
Prepare the required materials for thawing and ex vivo culture of PDTFs.
Add the matrix to the 96-well plate without touching the bottom or sides, on ice.
Setup a 6-well washing plate with pre-warmed tumor wash medium and place a Falcon cell strainer in the second well.
Thaw PDTFs in a cryovial, leaving a small clump of ice at the bottom.
Transfer any remaining fragments from the cryovial into a 50 mL tube using forceps.
Use forceps to transfer leftover PDTFs to the wall of the 50 mL tube for precise and fast thawing.
Add fragments to the center of the 96-well plate after the bottom layer of matrix has solidified.
Add a second layer of matrix on top of the fragments.
Pre-cool the 96-well plate on ice before usage.
Use Falcon Cell strainers, either 70 or 100 μm.
Use sterile fine-tipped forceps, with a separate pair for each tumor.
Prepare four 50 mL tubes per tumor.
Cool two of the 50 mL tubes on ice before use.
Pre-cool tumor medium on ice.
Pre-warm tumor wash medium to 37°C.
Calculate the total volume of the matrix using provided stock concentrations and final desired concentrations.
Determine the volume of collagen needed based on the final concentration and total volume of the matrix.
Calculate the volume of sodium bicarbonate required, which is 10% of the volume of collagen.
Prepare two pre-cooled 50 mL tubes.
Add ice-cold tumor medium to one tube.
Mix the collagen with 7.5% sodium bicarbonate in another tube by pipetting sodium bicarbonate first, then slowly adding collagen.
Pipette collagen using a p1000 tip or cut-off p200 pipet tip due to high viscosity.
Mix the calculated volume of cold tumor medium with the collagen-sodium bicarbonate mixture.
Fully dissolve Matrigel before transferring it into the 50 mL tube containing the matrix-tumor medium mix.
Transfer 40 μL of the matrix into each well of a pre-cooled 96-well flat bottom plate without introducing air bubbles.
Tap the plate carefully to spread the matrix throughout the well.
Incubate for 30 min at 37°C and 5% CO2 until the matrix is solid.
Hold the Matrigel tube at the top while resuspending sodium bicarbonate with collagen and tumor medium.
Slowly add the medium mix to the Matrigel to resuspend it in multiple steps, transferring back to the medium mix as needed.
Avoid making air bubbles during the resuspension of Matrigel.
Mix and cool the matrix before adding it to the 96-well plate.
Incubate for 15 min after step 22 (incubation with the first layer of matrix).
Start thawing tumor fragments after the 15-minute incubation.
Collect cryovials from the cryostorage on dry ice.
Add 7 mL of pre-warmed (37°C) wash medium to three wells of a 6-well plate.
Prepare two 50 mL Falcon tubes, one with a cell strainer.
Thaw the cryovials in a 37°C water bath until only a small clump of ice is visible.
Flick the tube and pour the content of the cryovial (fragments and freezing medium) into a 50 mL tube.
Remove any remaining fragments with forceps and place them on the rim of the 50 mL tube.
Flush the fragments with some wash medium before proceeding.
Add 10 mL of pre-warmed wash medium dropwise to the tube, one drop per second.
Swirl the tube gently to mix the fragments with the wash medium.
Pour the contents of the tube into a new 50 mL collection tube over a cell strainer.
Transfer the cell strainer containing fragments to the first well of a 6-well plate filled with wash medium.
Shake the fragments lightly for approximately 1–2 minutes in the first well.
Transfer the fragments using forceps to a new cell strainer in the second well.
Shake the fragments lightly for approximately 1–2 minutes in the second well.
Wash the fragments again in the third well by shaking them lightly for about 1–2 minutes.
Remove the fragments from the cell strainer with forceps and place them on the sterile part of the lid of the 6-well plate using a drop of medium.
Count the total number of fragments.
Transfer one fragment per well into a matrix-coated 96-well plate.
Cut fragments larger than 1 × 1 × 1 mm into smaller pieces.
Add 40 μL matrix mix to each tumor fragment.
Handle the plate at 20°C–22°C to keep the bottom layer of the matrix solidified.
Incubate for 30 min at 37°C and 5% CO2 until the matrix has solidified.
Add 120 μL tumor medium.
Incubate at 37°C and 5% CO2 for the required time period.
Mix 120 μL medium with any stimulation or treatment of interest.
Calculate the final concentration for a total volume of 200 μL.
Incubate the cultures at 37°C and 5% CO2 after adding the remaining 80 μL of medium.
Thaw a cryovial containing PDTFs.
Pour the contents into a 50 mL tube.
Add tumor wash medium dropwise to the tube.
Transfer any fragments stuck inside the cryotube to the 50 mL tube using forceps.
Flush fragments to the bottom of the tube with tumor wash medium.
Pour fragments over a cell strainer.
Wash fragments extensively in three wells of a 6-well plate.
Transfer fragments from one well to a new filter.
Divide fragments into different treatment conditions for ex vivo culture by transferring them in liquid to the lid of a plate prior to adding them to the matrix.
Incubate PDTFs embedded in matrix with treatment/stimulation for up to 48 hours (maximum 72 hours).
Collect supernatants from incubated PDTFs for analysis of soluble mediators.
Extract PDTFs from the matrix for imaging analyses or processing into single cell suspensions.
Process extracted PDTFs into single cell suspensions for flow cytometry or single-cell RNA-sequencing.
Prepare the following materials before starting:
Prepare one 15 mL tube with 2 mL digestion mix per condition and keep the tube(s) on ice.
Collect 80-100 μL of supernatant that is on top of the matrix in a 96-well round bottom plate after PDTF culture.
Seal the plate with the collected supernatants without further preparation.
Store the sealed plate at -80°C for later usage.
Tilt the plate when taking up the supernatant to avoid touching the tumor fragment and matrix.
Extract the tumor fragments from the matrix using forceps.
Transfer the extracted fragments directly into a 15 mL tube containing the digestion mix.
Pool fragments for each condition and mix them with the medium.
Leave the pooled fragments on ice until all conditions have been collected.
Place the tubes on a rotator and incubate at 37°C and 5% CO2 under slow rotation for 1 hour.
Check during incubation to ensure no fragments are sticking to the wall of the tube.
After digestion, keep the tube(s) on ice.
Top up each tube with ice-cold PBS.
Centrifuge at 235 × g for 10 minutes at 4°C.
Carefully remove the supernatant without disrupting the pellet and keep the tube(s) on ice.
Prepare a new 15 mL tube and place a nylon mesh filter on top.
Resuspend the cell pellet thoroughly with 5 mL of ice-cold PBS and filter the suspension through the mesh into the new 15 mL tube.
Centrifuge at 438 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Carefully remove the supernatant without disrupting the pellet.
Take a sample to count cell numbers and check viability if necessary.
Resuspend the cells in the medium of choice.
Retrieve supernatants from storage at -80°C and thaw them on ice.
Transfer the required volume from each well to the assay plate for analysis.
Mix supernatants from each well using equal volumes and pool them together.
Transfer the required volume from the pooled supernatants for the assay.
Refreeze pooled supernatants only once; avoid multiple freeze-thaw cycles.
